body:
Specialised physical science laboratories

Not every physical science laboratory in Gujarat conducts satellite research. Some investigate the behaviour of matter under unusual physical conditions, while others study the movement of the Earth. These institutions illustrate how a specialised scientific question determines the instruments, observations and expertise required.

Institute for Plasma Research

The Institute for Plasma Research (IPR) is located at Bhat, Gandhinagar, near the Sabarmati River. It was established as an autonomous research institute in 1986 and came under the administrative control of the Department of Atomic Energy, Government of India, in 1995.

Plasma is a state of matter containing electrically charged particles, including positive ions and free electrons. It is often described as the fourth state of matter, alongside solid, liquid and gas.

Plasma occurs naturally in the Sun and stars. It can also be produced under suitable conditions on Earth. Because charged particles respond to electric and magnetic fields, plasma behaves differently from an ordinary neutral gas.

IPR undertakes fundamental and applied research in plasma physics, including research related to nuclear fusion. In fusion, light atomic nuclei combine to form heavier nuclei, with energy released under suitable conditions. This is distinct from nuclear fission, in which a heavy atomic nucleus splits into smaller nuclei.

IPR's research facilities include the ADITYA-U (upgraded ADITYA) and SST-1 tokamak systems. A tokamak uses magnetic fields to confine plasma for research. These are experimental research facilities; they should not be described as ordinary commercial electricity-generating power stations.

Institute of Seismological Research

The Institute of Seismological Research (ISR) was established by the Government of Gujarat through a government resolution dated 27 August 2003. It is located at Raisan, Gandhinagar, and works in the field of earthquake science.

Seismology is the scientific study of earthquakes and seismic waves. An earthquake releases energy that travels through the Earth as seismic waves. Seismological instruments record ground movement and help researchers determine characteristics of an earthquake.

ISR undertakes earthquake monitoring, seismic hazard assessment and studies of faults and ground conditions. Its work supports understanding of earthquake risk and the development of information relevant to safer buildings and settlements.

Monitoring, hazard assessment and prediction are different

Earthquake monitoring records seismic activity. Seismic hazard assessment examines the likelihood and possible severity of ground shaking in an area over a specified period. Neither should be confused with a reliable prediction of the exact date, time, location and magnitude of a future earthquake, which current science cannot provide.

Earthquake research is especially relevant to Gujarat because the state includes earthquake-prone regions, notably Kachchh. Scientific observations help authorities and engineers understand hazards, but they cannot eliminate the underlying natural process.

Prelims focus

  • IPR is at Bhat, Gandhinagar.

  • ADITYA and SST-1 are associated with plasma research.

[Sources: Institute for Plasma Research, official 'History', 'Campuses' and plasma research information; Government of Gujarat, Department of Science and Technology, 'Institute of Seismological Research', Overview and institutional objectives. Consulted 3 November 2026.]

body:
How industrial research differs from basic research

Industrial research applies scientific knowledge to the development or improvement of materials, production methods and useful services. It may aim to improve product quality, reduce resource consumption, solve environmental problems or make an existing process more efficient.

Gujarat's coastline, agricultural activities, energy sector and dairy economy create important opportunities for applied research. Some institutions in these fields are central government research bodies, while others are state-supported organisations or national development institutions.

CSIR-Central Salt and Marine Chemicals Research Institute

The CSIR-Central Salt and Marine Chemicals Research Institute (CSIR-CSMCRI) is located in Bhavnagar. It was inaugurated on 10 April 1954 as the Central Salt Research Institute and subsequently developed into an institution concerned with salt and marine chemicals research.

It is a laboratory of the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR), a national research organisation. Its work concerns areas such as salt production and utilisation, marine chemicals, seaweed-related resources, membrane technology and the treatment or desalination of saline water.

Salt is important both as a food ingredient and as an industrial raw material. Research is needed because extracting and processing salt involves questions of purity, efficiency, environmental conditions and useful by-products.

Desalination means removing dissolved salts from saline water to obtain water suitable for a specified use. It does not mean that all untreated seawater is immediately suitable for drinking. The quality of the final water must meet the requirements of its intended use.

Gujarat Energy Research and Management Institute

The Gujarat Energy Research and Management Institute (GERMI) is based in the Gandhinagar area. It works on energy-related research, training, technical studies and management, including subjects associated with renewable energy.

Energy research is concerned with questions such as how energy is produced, converted, conserved and used efficiently. Research on solar energy, for example, may examine the performance of technology under different conditions. Its subject differs from the marine chemistry investigated at CSMCRI.

ICAR-Indian Institute of Groundnut Research

The ICAR-Indian Institute of Groundnut Research (IIGR), formerly the Directorate of Groundnut Research (DGR), is located at Junagadh and is associated with the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR). Its institutional origin dates to 1979.

Groundnut research investigates the crop's production and improvement. Important school-level scientific concerns include plant varieties, resistance to pests and diseases, environmental stresses and crop productivity. Research must account for differing agricultural conditions, rather than assuming that one method produces identical results in every field.

National Dairy Development Board

The National Dairy Development Board (NDDB) was founded in 1965 and is headquartered at Anand, Gujarat. It is a national dairy development institution, not merely an individual dairy-processing plant.

NDDB promotes dairy development through institutional support, scientific and technical services, animal breeding, animal health, nutrition, milk quality and dairy-related technology. Its work illustrates how biological and technological knowledge can support producers through organised systems.

NDDB is closely associated with Operation Flood, the major dairy development programme launched in 1970. The programme strengthened milk procurement and cooperative dairy development. NDDB and Amul should not be treated as interchangeable names: NDDB is a national development board, whereas Amul is associated with cooperative dairy marketing.

body:
What biotechnology means

Biotechnology involves using living organisms, cells or biological processes to develop useful products and services. Traditional examples include preparing curd through the action of microorganisms and using yeast in fermentation. Modern biotechnology also includes methods concerned with genetic material, biological molecules, diagnostics and the development of improved biological products.

Biotechnology has applications in healthcare, agriculture, industry and the environment. In healthcare, it can support disease diagnosis and the development of medicines. In agriculture, it may help researchers understand plant traits and disease resistance. Environmental applications can involve biological resources and the treatment of particular forms of waste.

Biotechnology is therefore broader than genetic engineering. Genetic engineering is one group of techniques within the wider field.

Gujarat State Biotechnology Mission

The Gujarat State Biotechnology Mission (GSBTM) was established in 2004 as part of Gujarat's effort to develop biotechnology. It works under the Department of Science and Technology, Government of Gujarat.

The mission's main role is to promote and support biotechnology development through coordination, policy-related activity, capacity building and connections among research institutions, industry and other participants. It is important to recognise GSBTM as a mission and coordinating organisation, rather than assuming that it is a university or a single specialised research laboratory.

Gujarat Biotechnology Research Centre

The Gujarat Biotechnology Research Centre (GBRC) is an autonomous research organisation established by the Gujarat government in 2017. Its government resolution was dated 11 August 2017, and its operations commenced on 1 September 2017. The centre is based in Gandhinagar.

GBRC conducts research directed towards problems involving healthcare, agriculture, environmental resources, industry and marine biotechnology. Its scientific capabilities include genomics, the study of genomes, and proteomics, the study of proteins on a broad scale.

These areas are useful because biological traits and processes depend on interactions involving genetic information and proteins. For example, genomic information can help researchers investigate the characteristics of a pathogen or a crop. However, identifying genetic information is not itself the same as developing an approved medicine or agricultural product.

GBRC also provides shared research facilities and supports collaboration with academic institutions, researchers, startups and industry.

Gujarat Biotechnology University

Gujarat Biotechnology University (GBU) is a state university established under Gujarat Act No. 16 of 2018. It is located at GIFT City, Gandhinagar, and is supported by the Gujarat Department of Science and Technology.

GBU provides advanced education and research opportunities in biotechnology. Its academic fields include animal, plant, medical, industrial and environmental biotechnology. It has an academic collaboration with the University of Edinburgh.

The distinction between GBRC and GBU is one of principal institutional purpose. GBRC is primarily a specialised research centre, whereas GBU is a university combining advanced teaching and research.

Gujarat Biotechnology Policy 2022–27

The Gujarat Biotechnology Policy 2022–27 concerns the development of the state's biotechnology sector, including investment, research-linked activity and industry. Its stated policy period covers 2022–2027.

As of 3 November 2026, this period has not ended. A policy's goals or incentives should be distinguished from completed projects and measured outcomes. The existence of a policy does not by itself establish that every planned investment or facility has been realised.

  • GSBTM was established in 2004 and is a state biotechnology promotion and coordination body.
  • GBRC was established in 2017 and is based in Gandhinagar.
  • GBRC's operations commenced on 1 September 2017.
  • GBU was created under Gujarat Act No. 16 of 2018.
  • GBU is located at GIFT City, Gandhinagar, and collaborates academically with the University of Edinburgh.
  • Trap: GSBTM, GBRC and GBU are distinct institutions with different principal roles.
